commitResults.messageTitle: Add Level-0 greeting and Mochi chatbot identity
Add Level-1 command echo and bye handling
Add Level-2 task storage and numbered listing
Add mark command for completed tasks
Add unmark command to restore pending status
Refactor Level-3 tasks into Task class
Add Level-4 todo, deadline, and event commands
Add Level-5 validation for invalid commands
Add Level-6 task deletion with index validation
Use Command enum for type-safe input dispatch

commitResults.messageBody: Tasks exist only for the duration of one Mochi process, so users lose their task list after exiting. Persist every task-list change to an OS-independent relative path and restore the stored tasks on startup. Handle missing storage paths automatically so first-time startup remains seamless.
Level-7 was developed and verified on its required feature branch. Merge the branch with an explicit merge commit so the course scripts can detect the branching workflow.

Deadline dates are stored as unvalidated text, which prevents Mochi from understanding invalid or impossible dates. Parse ISO dates into LocalDate values and format them for display while retaining ISO storage for reliable reloads.
Level-8 was developed and verified on its required feature branch. Merge it explicitly so the branch topology remains visible to the course scripts.

Task collection operations are mixed with application coordination. Move ownership of adding, retrieving, removing, sizing, and iterating tasks into TaskList so callers do not manage the underlying collection.
File loading and saving are application infrastructure concerns. Move them behind Storage so persistence format and file-system handling are isolated from the chatbot workflow.
Command validation and task construction obscure the main application flow. Centralize those responsibilities in Parser so parsing errors and formats have one owner.
Console reads and response formatting are scattered through the application. Move them into Ui so user interaction can evolve independently from command execution.

Mochi contains parsing, storage, collection, and display details despite those responsibilities now having dedicated classes. Reduce Mochi to coordinating Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList while preserving existing behavior.

The responsibility extractions were developed and regression-tested together on an isolated branch. Merge them explicitly to keep the multi-step refactor visible while returning master to a verified state.

All classes share the default package, which hides subsystem boundaries and becomes harder to navigate as the project grows. Group application, command, exception, parser, storage, task, and UI classes under the mochi namespace while preserving src/main/java as the source root.
The package reorganization was compiled and regression-tested on its feature branch. Merge it explicitly to keep master at a verified checkpoint.
